Article Title: Trump, Xi, Putin agree on UN reforms: What it means for India's permanent UNSC seat bid
Article Text:
What was discussed at the trilateral meeting

India's long-standing demand for a seat at the high table

China-Pakistan opposition remains a major hurdle

Is the new agreement a window of opportunity for India?

The world looks very different today from what it did when the United Nations was established in 1945. The global order has shifted from bipolar to increasingly multipolar, relations between countries have changed, and several new nations have emerged while others have ceased to exist.Yet, the exclusive club of five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has remained unchanged, despite longstanding calls for its expansion to give countries like India a greater say in global affairs.Thursday offered a possible glimpse of change in the global governance system as US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen, bringing together the leaders of three of the five permanent members of the UNSC.While the meeting covered several issues, what stood out was their stated commitment to reforming the United Nations.But could this open a window for India's decades-long ambition of securing a permanent seat at the high table, or will the existing power equations continue to stand in its way?Three of the world's most powerful leaders met at a time of deep geopolitical divisions. After around 80 minutes of talks, they emerged with commitments to reform the United Nations, increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products, and hold discussions on reducing nuclear risks.According to the joint statement titled "Declaration toward Peace", the three leaders held an in-depth exchange of views on the international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security.The first point of the declaration addressed reform of the United Nations."As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, Russia, China and the United States committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security," the statement read.The agreement has brought New Delhi's longstanding demand for a permanent seat on the Security Council back into focus.However, there is an important distinction. The declaration calls for reform of the UN but stops short of spelling out what those reforms would entail or whether they would include an expansion of the Security Council's permanent membership.That leaves a crucial question unanswered: Are the three powers willing to change the institution's existing power structure, or do they envision reforms that leave their own privileged positions untouched?India, a founding member of the United Nations, has sought a permanent seat on the Security Council for decades. New Delhi's central argument is that a world body created in the aftermath of World War II cannot adequately represent today's world without giving India, the most populous country, a major economy, a leading democracy and a significant contributor to UN peacekeeping operations, a permanent place at the decision-making table.In 1994, India formally announced its candidature for permanent membership at the 49th UN General Assembly and has consistently reiterated its demand since.However, securing a permanent seat is not simply a matter of obtaining support from a majority of countries.Any expansion of the Security Council's permanent membership would require an amendment to the UN Charter under Article 108. This needs approval by a two-thirds majority in the 193-member General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of UN member states, including all five existing permanent members — the US, UK, France, Russia and China.In effect, each of the five permanent members has the power to prevent such an amendment from taking effect, making their consent essential to any expansion.In September this year, external affairs minister S Jaishankar joined his counterparts from Brazil, Germany and Japan, collectively known as the G4, to call for early reform of the Council and expansion in both permanent and non-permanent categories.In a press release, the ministry of external affairs said the G4 ministers emphasised that "it is crucial to implement UNSC reform at the earliest so that the Council is fit-for-purpose, truly reflecting contemporary geopolitical realities.""They underscored that expansion of the UNSC in both the permanent and non-permanent categories of membership is central to such reform and that this position is supported by a majority of member states. In this context, they reiterated the importance of improving the representation of the underrepresented and unrepresented regions and groups, such as Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America and the Caribbean, in both these categories," the statement read.India has also voiced similar concerns through the IBSA grouping with Brazil and South Africa. A joint statement supported "transformative" UNSC reform, permanent seats for India and Brazil, and Africa's aspiration for permanent representation. It also called for a fixed timetable and text-based negotiations during the 81st UN General Assembly.Jaishankar has repeatedly argued that India's exclusion is not merely a setback for New Delhi but also a problem for the credibility of the United Nations itself."To have such a country not there in the key global councils, obviously, it's not good for us, but I would also urge it's not good for the global Council in question," Jaishankar said in 2022.While India has continued to push for a permanent seat on the Security Council, opposition from China and Pakistan remains among the biggest obstacles to its candidature.Beijing has supported Security Council reform in principle but has stopped short of endorsing India's individual candidature.China has maintained that reforms should focus on improving the representation of developing countries, particularly African nations, rather than simply adding a small number of new permanent members.During UN discussions, Chinese representatives have argued that the reform process should not be reduced to the individual aspirations of countries seeking permanent membership.In November 2022, China's then Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Zhang Jun, opposed the adoption of a negotiating text or a timetable for UNSC reform. He warned that such a move could lead to "conflicts" and even "derail the process".Zhang also criticised countries seeking permanent membership to enhance their international standing, in remarks widely seen as an indirect reference to India and the G4."Some countries had their own agenda for reforms, seeking permanent membership to enhance their international standing," he said.Pakistan, meanwhile, is a leading member of the Uniting for Consensus group, also known as the Coffee Club, which opposes the creation of new permanent seats and favours expanding the elected, non-permanent category of membership.Unlike China, Pakistan is not a permanent member and cannot independently block an amendment to the UN Charter through the ratification requirement. However, it can oppose India's candidature through diplomatic negotiations and coalition-building within the General Assembly.The two countries' positions, along with differences among the existing permanent members, have complicated efforts to reach an agreement on the future composition of the Security Council.Speaking to The Times of India, Jawaharlal Nehru University professor Rajan Kumar described the recent summit between the three leaders as more of a diplomatic gesture than a serious commitment to concrete changes in the global governance system."It is a major development that the three countries have met to discuss UN reform, but I believe it is more of a lip service than a serious commitment towards taking any concrete steps towards oil supply chain, nuclear disarmament, reform in the global governance system," he said.Kumar argued that despite agreeing on the need for reforms, the three countries have little common ground when it comes to changing the existing power structure of the Security Council.According to him, their competing geopolitical interests make it difficult to expect a consensus on expanding permanent membership, particularly when the existing arrangement gives them considerable influence over international decision-making."All three countries are opposed to expanding the UNSC. Moreover, the US, Russia and China often use their veto power against each other on issues at the Security Council. When the US raises an issue, China and Russia often align against it, and vice versa. So, do you really expect them to reach a consensus on expanding the UNSC to accommodate countries like Brazil and India?" he asked.The concern is that while the three countries may agree on the broad need to make the United Nations more effective, they have little incentive to support changes that could dilute their own influence.The Shenzhen declaration has certainly brought the question of UN reform back into the conversation. However, without a specific proposal for Security Council expansion or a commitment from the permanent members to support it, there is little to suggest that the existing power structure is about to change.For India, the agreement may offer a glimmer of hope, but its decades-long ambition of securing a permanent seat remains a distant prospect.The three powers have agreed that the United Nations needs reform. Whether they are willing to share the power that comes with permanent membership is an entirely different question.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen. The meeting covered several issues, but what stood out was their stated commitment to reforming the United Nations. Could this open a window for India's decades-long ambition of securing a permanent seat at the high table?

Article Title: 'Will find way forward through dialogue': Amit Shah assures Arunachal locals amid Siang dam protests
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah in Arunachal Pradesh

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah , who is visiting Arunachal Pradesh amid protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), assured locals on Saturday that the Centre would protect their traditions, culture and religious beliefs."I am aware of the sentiments and apprehensions of the people of Siang region, and I have come to Arunachal Pradesh to address your concerns directly," Shah said at the Police Training Centre in Banderdewa, near state capital Itanagar.Acknowledging that some of the concerns raised were "significant", Shah assured residents that the government was aware of the aspirations of local communities."I want to assure my brothers and sisters from Siang that we will find a way forward through positive dialogue ... You need not worry about it. The government and I have the same respect you have for the local culture. We will move forward without compromising the traditions, culture and religion of this place," he added.The home minister, whose remarks mark his first public statement on the issue, urged people to engage with the Arunachal Pradesh government and convey their concerns to the Union home ministry through the state administration.Shah's assurance comes amid continued opposition to the proposed mega dam from sections of the indigenous Adi community, particularly residents of Siang and Upper Siang districts. They have expressed concerns over its possible impact on their ancestral lands, villages, livelihood, environment and cultural identity.The project, proposed on the Siang River, is considered strategically important by the Centre, particularly in view of China's plans to develop a massive hydropower project on the upper reaches of the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet. The river enters India as the Siang before flowing into Assam as the Brahmaputra.The project is envisaged not only as a major source of hydroelectric power but also as a strategic intervention to strengthen India's energy and water security. It is expected to help regulate river flows, besides providing Arunachal Pradesh with opportunities for revenue generation, infrastructure development and employment.However, indigenous organisations and local residents have questioned the need for such a massive project, citing the fragile ecology of the Siang Valley and the possible consequences of large-scale construction in a seismically sensitive region.They have also alleged that adequate public consultation has not taken place and demanded greater transparency in the ongoing pre-feasibility report exercise.For many Adi families, the Siang River is not merely a source of livelihood but is closely linked to their history, traditional beliefs and cultural practices.Protests against the project have intensified in recent months, with indigenous groups demanding that the government reconsider the proposal and ensure that the concerns of the affected communities are addressed before proceeding further.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah is visiting Arunachal Pradesh amid protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. Shah assured locals on Saturday that the Centre would protect their traditions, culture and religious beliefs.

Article Text:
India, France condemn Pak-sponsored terror attack

NEW DELHI: India and France have condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including crossborder terrorism and violent extremism, and agreed to strengthen cooperation to tackle terror financing, online radicalisation and emerging technological threats.The two countries reiterated their strong condemnation of the April 22, 2025, terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, and the November 2025 terror incident near the Red Fort in New Delhi during the 18th meeting of the India-France Joint Working Group (JWG) on Counter Terrorism held in New Delhi on November 20.According to a ministry of external affairs (MEA) press release, the meeting was co-chaired by Suhel Ajaz Khan, Additional Secretary (Counter Terrorism) in the MEA, and Olivier Caron, French Ambassador-at-Large and Special Envoy for Counter-Terrorism and Organised Crime.During the discussions, both sides exchanged views on the prevailing terror threat in their respective regions and at the global level, including challenges posed by state-sponsored and cross-border terrorism.The two delegations also discussed ways to tackle traditional and emerging security challenges, particularly the misuse of new technologies and financial technologies by terrorist groups.The Indian side briefed the French delegation on its comprehensive National Counter Terrorism Policy and Strategy, PRAHAAR.Both countries also explored ways to deepen bilateral cooperation in combating terrorism through information sharing, capacity-building, training and the exchange of experiences and best practices. They also discussed measures to counter terror financing and online radicalisation.The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in multilateral forums, including the United Nations, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the No Money for Terror (NMFT) initiative.The meeting concluded with both sides agreeing to hold the 19th meeting of the Joint Working Group in France on a mutually convenient date.The discussions reaffirmed India and France's commitment to stepping up joint efforts to counter terrorism and address evolving security challenges.
Article Summary: India and France have condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. They agreed to strengthen cooperation to tackle terror financing, online radicalisation and emerging technological threats. Both sides agreed to hold the 19th meeting of the Joint Working Group in France on a mutually convenient date.

Article Title: 'Sonia Gandhi was real owner of Maruti': BJP's Nishikant Dubey makes big claim; raises questions over '1970 deal'
Article Text:
Maruti, Indira Gandhi and Sonia: BJP's Nishikant Dubey raises questions over company's origins

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party MP Nishikant Dubey on Saturday levelled a series of allegations against senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi . Godda MP questioned former Congress chief alleged ownership, shareholding and appointment in Maruti-related entities.In a post on X, Dubey referred to the formation of the company and its alleged links with the Congress government led by former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi .Describing Sonia Gandhi as the "real owner of Maruti ", the BJP MP questioned how she allegedly held a position in the company despite being a foreign national.Referring to November 21, 1970, Dubey claimed that Sanjay Gandhi had entered into an agreement with Maruti Technical Services Private Limited, which he alleged was associated with Sonia Gandhi. He also questioned how the company received government authorisation to manufacture cars in 1968, despite being established in 1970."Did you know that despite being a foreign national, Sonia Gandhi was the Managing Director and 50 per cent shareholder of Maruti? On November 21, 1970, Sanjay Gandhi entered into an agreement with Sonia Gandhi’s Maruti Technical Services Private Limited. Sonia Gandhi was the real owner of Maruti.The Maruti company was established in 1970, but it had already received a letter from the Government of India in 1968 authorising it to manufacture cars," Dubey wrote.He further questioned how Sonia Gandhi allegedly became a director of the company in 1970, claiming that government rules did not permit foreign nationals to become directors of Indian companies.Dubey also linked the issue to the nationalisation of banks, alleging that the move was intended to facilitate loans to companies associated with Sonia Gandhi."In 1969, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi issued a Cabinet order allowing her daughter-in-law, Sonia Gandhi’s company, to manufacture cars? On April 3, 1972, Sanjay Gandhi travelled around the world at the Government of India’s expense for the company? How did Sonia Gandhi become this company’s Managing Director and 50 per cent owner? Under the Government of India’s rules, no foreign national could become a director of an Indian company? How did she become a director in 1970? Wasn’t the nationalisation of banks done solely to provide loans to her companies? Under Haryana government rules at the time, land could not be allotted in a foreign national’s name, yet Sonia Gandhi was allotted land in 1970?", he wrote.The BJP MP also raised questions about the alleged involvement of the Prime Minister's Office and government agencies in the company's operations."How was a private company’s office opened in the Prime Minister’s Office? How did the Prime Minister’s private secretary, Mr Dhawan, become its director? On the Prime Minister’s direct orders, before the company even existed, did all state governments make advance payments to Maruti to build bus bodies? How did government companies supply cement, steel, and coal directly to Maruti without payment?" he continued.Concluding his post, Dubey challenged Sonia Gandhi to explain the company's origins and alleged that it had been handed over to her by Indira Gandhi without any investment from her."If only Sonia ji would explain in her book how she built a large company without investing her own money, and how Prime Minister Indira Gandhi handed her the Maruti company as a favor," he wrote.The remarks come amid a political exchange over Sonia Gandhi's recently released memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', published on November 10.The book has triggered a war of words between the BJP and Congress, with the ruling party accusing Sonia of attempting to whitewash controversial chapters of her family's political history, including the 1975 Emergency and the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.
Article Summary: Bharatiya Janata Party MP Nishikant Dubey questions former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi's ownership, shareholding and appointment in Maruti-related entities. Dubey referred to the formation of the company and its alleged links with the Congress government led by former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. He questioned how the company received government authorisation to manufacture cars in 1968, despite being established in 1970.

Article Title: Consider law to curb marriage between relatives: SC to government
Article Text:
govt must explore the legislative route to prevent marriage between close relatives

NEW DELHI: The ordeal of a 20-year-old Bengaluru-based woman who defied serious physical conditions to gain admission to an elite law school became the trigger for a fresh Supreme Court push for a uniform civil code (UCC).Moved by her plight, the court said Friday the Union govt must explore the legislative route to prevent marriage between close relatives, prevalent among Muslims and some Hindu communities in the south, to protect their offspring against genetic disorders.Born to parents who are first cousins, the LLB student at National Law School of India University who suffers from genetic disorders photophobia and cone dystrophy, pleaded in her PIL that exceptions carved out to allow marriage between close relatives must be ended to give offspring the right to a healthy life."Should the law continue to retain statutory and customary exceptions that permit marriages between close blood relatives, notwithstanding established medical evidence that such unions significantly increase risk of autosomal recessive disorders, congenital anomalies, disabilities, infant morbidity and other lifelong health issues in children?" she asked.Photophobia is an abnormal intolerance of light, while cone dystrophy causes breakdown of cone photoreceptor cells in the retina.Children in marriages between close relatives are at greater risk of inheriting two copies of the altered recessive gene from the parents, leading to genetic disorders.The PIL challenged the custom-based exceptions preserved in Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, and Special Marriage Act, 1954.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was convinced the problem would be best addressed through the legislative route rather than a symptomatic judicial antidote.Quoting National Family Health Survey data, the petitioner said consanguineous marriages (marriages between people related by blood) were deeply entrenched in cultural, religious and social practices. According to NFHS, "13% of ever-married women were related to their husband before their marriage, and 11% of marriages were consanguineous marriages. The most common type of consanguineous marriages were marriages to first cousins (8% of all marriages). "The survey said, "Women in urban areas are about equally as likely to be in consanguineous marriages as women in rural areas. Muslim and Buddhist/Neo-Buddhist women are the most likely to be in consanguineous marriages." It had put the rate of such marriages among Muslims at 15.8%, among Buddhists/Neo-Buddhists at 14.5%, among Christians at 11.9%, and among Hindus at 10.1%.The survey further said, "Women in all southern states except Kerala are much more likely to be in consanguineous marriages than women in other states. More than one-fourth of women in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, and almost one-fifth of women in Telangana and Puducherry reported being in consanguineous marriages."The bench sought Centre's response on two aspects - the desirability of legislation to prevent consanguineous marriages, and an awareness campaign on possible adverse genetic disorders afflicting children from marriage between blood relatives, including making it a part of school and college curricula.The petitioner said, "Children should not be subjected to preventable and irreversible genetic risks, especially when the law continues to defer to custom where constitutional protection, public health and child welfare are at stake.""Consanguineous marriages pose a... demonstrable threat to public health, particularly to the right to life and health of children born out of such unions, who are disproportionately susceptible to congenital and genetic disorders bey-ond their control," she said.
Article Summary: 20-year-old Bengaluru-based woman defied serious physical conditions to gain admission to an elite law school. Court said Friday the Union govt must explore the legislative route to prevent marriage between close relatives. Consanguineous marriages are prevalent among Muslims and some Hindu communities in the south.

Article Title: No brakes required: How India's highways are now charging toll without stopping you
Article Text:
Inside India’s biggest toll overhaul since FASTag

How the system works

Six months, seven plazas

What happens when the payment fails

The early numbers

What the government expects to save

Passes for the frequent traveller

The risks that remain

The road ahead

For two decades the toll plaza has been a fixture of the Indian highway: the slowing down, the queue, the wait for a barrier to lift. Over the past six months, at a handful of locations across the country, that routine has started to disappear. Vehicles now pass under overhead gantries without stopping, and the toll is settled electronically afterwards.The technology is called Multi-Lane Free Flow, or MLFF. It lets vehicles pass through toll locations without stopping. It is still a small part of a very large network, but it marks the biggest change in how India collects highway tolls since FASTag made cashless payment routine.MLFF does not replace FASTag. It builds on it. The framework combines Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) with FASTag-based electronic collection: cameras read number plates as vehicles pass under gantries, and the FASTag account is debited automatically. Because of the “One Vehicle, One Tag” policy, each FASTag is tied to a vehicle’s registration number, so the equipment can create a toll transaction by reading the tag, the number plate, or both.The government says the aim is a faster and cleaner journey. NHAI says the technology should cut travel time, improve fuel efficiency, and make road transport safer and more sustainable.The first site went live on 1 May 2026. NHAI announced India’s first MLFF system at the Chorayasi Toll Plaza on the Surat–Bharuch section of NH-48 in Gujarat.Mundka-Bakkarwala on the Urban Extension Road-II in the Delhi-NCR region followed as the second. Union Minister Nitin Gadkari inaugurated it.The summer brought more. Rajasthan’s first MLFF plaza opened at Daulatpura on the Delhi–Jaipur section of NH-48 on 19 June. Gharaunda on the Panipat–Jalandhar section of NH-44 came next, and Manoharpura on the Delhi–Jaipur road followed on 1 July. Shahjahanpur, also on NH-48 in Rajasthan, went live in August. With that, all three plazas on the corridor supported non-stop passage. The system then moved south. On 1 October, NHAI rolled out Tamil Nadu’s first MLFF system at Paranur Toll Plaza on the Tambaram–Tindivanam section of NH-179B. Seven plazas are now operational.That is slower than planned. NHAI had targeted 17 plazas across nine states by September 2026.The harder question is what happens when the FASTag does not work. Without a booth, there is no one to stop the vehicle. The framework answers this with an electronic notice, or e-notice.If the FASTag balance is insufficient, or the tag is invalid or non-functional, the motorist is issued an e-notice and must pay the normal fee within 72 hours. After that, the amount is charged at twice the normal rate for the vehicle category. The notice is sent by SMS to the mobile number registered against the vehicle in the VAHAN database, and to the number linked to the FASTag. The mechanism rests on Rule 14 of the National Highway Fee Rules, 2008.Notices can be checked and paid on the designated portal, and a grievance can be raised there within the same 72 hours. The e-notice can also be viewed on the Rajmargyatra mobile app. The stakes of ignoring one go beyond the doubled fee. Non-payment may lead to the FASTag being blacklisted and to restrictions on other vehicle-related services through the VAHAN platform.multi lane free flow mlff barrierless tolling what to know features how to check enoticeNHAI’s advice to motorists is plain. Keep the FASTag balance sufficient, keep the tag active and properly affixed on the windshield, and use a clear High Security Registration Plate, whose laser-etched serial number the ANPR cameras can read.A Crisil Intelligence analysis gives the first real measure of how the system is performing. By 1 August, six plazas had together processed more than 110 lakh vehicle transactions and collected over Rs 147 crore in toll revenue since Choryasi opened. Choryasi led on revenue at more than Rs 51 crore, while Mundka handled the highest volume, at over 41.5 lakh transactions.FASTag is still doing most of the work. It accounted for roughly 94 per cent of revenue between May and July, about Rs 138.4 crore, against Rs 9.2 crore collected through e-notices. The notice figures show how large the compliance problem is. About 10 per cent of vehicles passing through the operational plazas triggered a payment failure, roughly 10.5 lakh notices in all.The ministry’s case rests on money, fuel and emissions. It expects MLFF to cut operational costs by Rs 5,000–6,000 crore a year and save around 250 crore litres of fuel annually, which it puts at nearly 81,000 tonnes less CO2, mainly by reducing idling and congestion at toll points. Once fully rolled out, the system is projected to handle more than 450 crore vehicle passages a year.The current network is a pilot compared with what is planned. NHAI has invited bids to extend MLFF to 104 more plazas across Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Gujarat and Rajasthan. Combined with plazas already operational or awarded, that would bring the total to 121. That is only 10–11 per cent of the more than 1,150 physical plazas now active nationwide.The shift comes alongside changes to how regular users pay. The annual FASTag pass, launched in August 2025, was being used by around 52 per cent of private vehicles at these plazas. Its standard price is Rs 3,075.A cheaper option for people who live near plazas took effect on 1 November. The ministry introduced a Concessional Local Pass for eligible non-commercial vehicle owners living within 20 km of a fee plaza. It costs Rs 1,500 a year at plazas outside municipal or local town limits and Rs 3,000 at those within them. Eligible owners with a valid, working FASTag can choose between this and the existing monthly pass. The pass is valid only at the plaza for which it is issued and cannot be transferred.Officials expect it to encourage more commuters to link their vehicles to FASTag, and so reduce e-notices.The Crisil analysis lists the system’s weak points. It points to revenue leakage from payment failures, inaccurate vehicle identification and tampered tags, and calls for stronger ANPR camera coverage and tighter integration with the VAHAN registry.There is also the matter of the motorist who never sees the notice. The 72-hour window is short, and the penalty is a doubled fee and, potentially, a blacklisted tag. A vehicle owner whose registered mobile number is out of date, or who does not check SMS regularly, is the person most exposed. That is a question for the next phase as much as for the first.India’s highway toll system is changing in stages. FASTag took the cash out of the booth. MLFF now aims to take out the booth itself. Seven plazas, an expanding bid pipeline and a first set of figures show the direction of travel, but the pace is behind the original target, and a network of over 1,150 plazas will not change quickly.What the next phase has to show is whether the compliance rate improves as more motorists link their tags and plates correctly, and whether the savings the ministry projects begin to show at the plazas that have already gone live.
Article Summary: Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) lets vehicles pass through toll locations without stopping. It is still a small part of a very large network, but it marks the biggest change in how India collects highway tolls since FASTag made cashless payment routine.

Article Title: First regular India-Nepal passenger train to link birthplaces of Lord Ram and Mata Sita
Article Text:
India and Nepal are preparing to inaugurate a direct train service linking Ayodhya and Janakpur.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: After a gap over two years, Indian railways will run a direct cross-border passenger train. This time to Nepal, to link Lord Ram’s birthplace Ayodhya to that of Mata Sita’s in Janakpur. The move will not only connect the two cities revered by Hindus, promoting religious tourism, but also play the larger role of strengthening bilateral relations.TOI has learnt that PM Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah will virtually flag off the train on its inaugural run on Nov 23 (Monday). As per a railway ministry notification, the weekly train from Janakpur will depart every Saturday afternoon while departure from Ayodhya will be every Monday afternoon.The last cross-border trains that India operated were Maitree and Bandhan Express to Bangladesh. The services were suspended indefinitely in July-Aug 2024 following violent protests and political turmoil in the neighbouring nation. There is no sign of the operation resuming anytime soon.Earlier, India’s passenger train services to Pakistan — Samjhauta Express and Thar Express — were suspended in Aug 2019 after govt revoked J&K’s special status under Article 320 and the subsequent deterioration in bilateral relations.So, the direct train to Janakpur will be the only active cross-border link from India in the region.“This will be the first direct passenger train from India to Nepal.At present, passengers from India can travel up to Jaynagar station in Bihar by Indian Railways, then they need to undergo customs clearance and board trains run by Nepal Railways to reach Janakpur Dham and Kurtha in Nepal. However, in the case of Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham train, passengers will continue to travel in the same train after customs clearance,” said an official.The one-way journey of around 604 km will take approximately 19 hours. The train with AC2, AC3 and sleeper coaches can accommodate around 1,100 passengers. The train will stop at stations including Mankapur, Basti, Gorakhpur, Narkatiaganj, Raxaul, Sitamarhi, Shisho, Madhubani and Jaynagar. Indian passengers need to carry a valid proof such as passport, voter-id, Aadhaar or driving licence.
Article Summary: India and Nepal are preparing to inaugurate a direct train service linking Ayodhya and Janakpur. The move will not only connect the two cities revered by Hindus, promoting religious tourism, but also play the larger role of strengthening bilateral relations. PM Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah will virtually flag off the train on its inaugural run on Nov 23.

Article Title: CBI Recovers Cash and jewellery from CGST Superintendent home
Article Text:
CBI Recovers Cash and jewellery from CGST Superintendent

NEW DELHI: Central Bureau of Investigation ( CBI ) has recovered cash, foreign currency, gold and silver worth approximately Rs 1.8 crore during searches conducted at the residential premises of a Superintendent of Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST), posted at Panchkula, Haryana, who was arrested in a bribery case on Nov 19.The CBI had registered the case against the accused Superintendent on allegations of demanding illegal gratification for extending undue favour in GST proceedings against a private firm. The accused was caught red-handed while accepting a bribe of Rs 10 lakh from the complainant during a trap laid at Panchkula.During subsequent searches conducted on Nov 20, Indian currency amounting to Rs 24.2 lakh, foreign currency equivalent to approximately Rs 15.6 lakh, and gold jewellery, gold bullion and silver collectively valued at approximately Rs. 1.4 crore were recovered. The total value of these recoveries is approximately Rs. 1.8 crore.The searches also led to the recovery of documents relating to six bank accounts, investment portfolios, a life insurance policy and multiple immovable properties. Article Title: Government avoids war of words, fears extradition push is a delaying tactic
Article Text:

Government declined to comment on remarks made by Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman blaming India and the Awami League led by former PM Sheikh Hasina for a fresh wave of unrest in the country, choosing not to get drawn into the political rhetoric emerging from Dhaka."Our position remains consistent that India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh, one which is rooted in the shared histories of the two countries and in their shared cultural ties of their peoples. I have no comments to make on the internal developments in Bangladesh," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.However, while maintaining so far that the Hasina passport issue is between Dhaka and the former PM, the government suspects that Dhaka's insistence on her return only under the extradition treaty might be a stalling tactic to avoid confronting political risks and security challenges of keeping her in custody.Hasina renewed her passport and national identity card request this week through a 'signed' letter which was promptly turned down. Bangladesh has also questioned the authenticity of the letter. For India, the issue of her extradition is distinct from the passport request and the 2 should not be conflated, as extradition is a mechanism to compel the return only of a person who is resisting going back.India sees the issue of passport as a question of Bangladesh's own laws and its obligations towards a citizen.It also believes though that with Hasina seemingly ready to return to Dhaka of her own volition, there may not be any case for her extradition, which in any case is going to be a complicated legal process. For India, the lack of a travel document is the only thing blocking voluntary Hasina's return as New Delhi is unlikely to do anything to block it.Government considers significant many international conventions that Bangladesh is also a party to refer explicitly to a person’s right to return to his/her own country. Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) Article 15 recognises the right to a nationality and bars its arbitrary deprivation. Article 13(2) also recognises the right to leave and return to one’s country. While UDHR is not a legally binding instrument, it's seen as setting important standards.Similarly, International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) Article 12(4) shields against arbitrary deprivation of the right to enter one’s own country.Government also sees as misconceived the argument about "convicted criminal” passport restriction as it is an exit-control provision and not an entry-control tool. According to authorities here, a citizen reserves the right to return to his/her own country and this cannot be framed as a procedural step to be processed through a treaty.
Article Summary: Government declined to comment on remarks made by Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman blaming India and the Awami League led by former PM Sheikh Hasina for a fresh wave of unrest in the country. We need to treasure those," he said emphasising the need to preserve the collection, which includes material dating back to the 17th century.Justice Kumar also recalled a 2009 fire at the Hyderabad High Court library, which destroyed historic books and deeply affected the then chief justice, Justice A R Dave.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta agreed with the bench's concerns, saying the government was aware of the importance of preserving the collection.Citing the ancient Nalanda library, he said, "It's a treasure which we may lose. We are conscious and the government is also conscious of the fact."Mehta assured the court that the Centre would honour its undertaking. He also said officials would meet with the amicus curiae to work out a solution.Earlier on November 16, the Supreme Court had pulled up the Centre over the proposed relocation, questioning the lack of adequate arrangements for the library's books and expressing concern over their preservation.Earlier, on October 5, the court had sought the actual layout plan and details of the space proposed for the library in the new Central Vista complex.The Centre had told the bench that the library, which currently occupies 4,144 square metres, would be allotted around 5,200 square metres.The court had also sought an affidavit clarifying whether the proposed space would accommodate books currently housed at Shastri Bhawan as well as those lying unopened in cartons at RK Puram since 2011.The library has been housed across four floors of Shastri Bhawan since 1969.Following reports that only two rooms had been allotted to it in Kartavya Bhawan-2, the Union housing ministry had clarified that space had been provided for the library under the Central Vista redevelopment plan and that the construction process was underway.
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders suo motu case concerning the proposed relocation of the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library in Delhi. Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva said the matter did not fall under its current roster and should be placed before the CJI.

Article Title: ‘Dialogue on civilisation, not war’: PM Modi's message at SCO summit - top quotes
Article Text:
PM Modi says SCO civilisational forum can give direction to world

Here are the top quotes:

At a time when discussions about war and unrest dominate the world, we are engaging in a dialogue on civilisational connections in India. Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites
