Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Raipur couple files Rs 7.28 lakh medical claim, National Insurance rejects it over non-disclosure of heart condition; consumer commission orders insurer to pay Rs 5.46 lakh, Rs 50,000 compensation and
Article Text:
(AI image) The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Raipur ruled that National Insurance Company must pay an insured couple





RAIPUR: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Raipur, has directed National Insurance Company Ltd to pay Rs 5.46 lakh towards medical expenses incurred by an insured couple, holding the insurance company's rejection of their claim under a National Super Top-up Mediclaim Policy to be unjustified.The commission, comprising president Prashant Kundu and member Dr Anand Varghese, partly allowed a consumer complaint filed by Madhukant Agrawal and his wife, directing the insurer to pay 75% of the claimed medical expenses of Rs 7.28 lakh within 45 days. It also awarded Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental agony and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.The commission further directed that if the insurer failed to make the payments within the stipulated 45 days, it would have to pay interest at 7% per annum on the entire awarded amount from the date of the order until payment.According to the complaint, the couple had obtained a mediclaim policy from National Insurance Company in 2017 and subsequently purchased a National Super Top-up Mediclaim Policy. The latter policy was valid from Sept 22, 2024, to Sept 21, 2025.The complainant's wife suffered a heart attack on Aug 10, 2024, and was admitted to a private hospital in Raipur, where doctors conducted angiography and advised further treatment for blockages in her coronary arteries.On medical advice, she was shifted to a private hospital in Hyderabad on Aug 20, 2024, where she underwent surgery on Aug 23. After being discharged, she continued to experience complications and underwent further treatment at hospitals in Hyderabad and Kochi.The couple stated that medical treatment continued until March 2025 and that they incurred substantial expenses. They submitted claims under their insurance policies. While the insurer paid Rs 4 lakh under the basic mediclaim policy, it rejected the claim under the Super Top-up policy, citing alleged non-disclosure of the insured woman's pre-existing heart condition.The complainants contended that the rejection was arbitrary and amounted to deficiency in service and unfair treatment. They sought reimbursement of the outstanding Rs 7.28 lakh, Rs 2 lakh as compensation for mental agony and litigation expenses.The insurance company, however, maintained that the complainants had concealed relevant medical information while obtaining the Super Top-up policy and that the claim was not payable under its terms and conditions.After examining the affidavits, insurance documents, medical records, hospital bills and other evidence, the commission considered the policy terms and the circumstances surrounding the treatment and claim rejection.It noted that the basic mediclaim policy had been continuously renewed since 2017 and that the Super Top-up policy was a separate insurance cover. The commission also examined clause 4.1 of the Super Top-up policy concerning the admissibility of claims based on the period of coverage.The commission concluded that the insurer's rejection of the claim was not justified to the extent of the amount payable under the applicable policy provisions. It held that the complainants were entitled to 75% of the outstanding medical expense claim of Rs 7.28 lakh, amounting to Rs 5.46 lakh.The complaint was partly allowed under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, with directions for payment of the awarded amounts within 45 day.
Article Summary: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Raipur, has directed National Insurance Company Ltd to pay Rs 5.46 lakh towards medical expenses incurred by an insured couple. The commission, comprising president Prashant Kundu and member Dr Anand Varghese, partly allowed a complaint filed by Madhukant Agrawal and his wife.

Article Title: Bengaluru man suffers nose injury after Metro grab handle snaps mid-journey, breaks Rs 3,000 spectacles; BMRCL claims passenger put entire body weight on handle but fails to produce CCTV footage, cons
Article Text:
AI generated image used for representational purpose only





BENGALURU: A routine Metro commute turned painful for a 49-year-old Bengaluru man when a grab handle inside a crowded train snapped and struck him on the nose, leaving him bleeding and damaging his spectacles. After the Metro operator denied responsibility and refused medical compensation, he approached a consumer commission, which has now held Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (BMRCL) liable for deficiency in service.The incident took place on January 18, 2025, when MG Nagaraju, a resident of Ganga Nagar Extension, boarded a Metro train from Rajajinagar to KR Market using his Metro card. With all seats occupied, he stood holding a grab handle for support.As the train approached KR Market station, the handle suddenly snapped and hit him on the nose, causing severe bleeding. The impact also broke his spectacles, worth Rs 3,000, and nearly sent him tumbling inside the moving coach. Fellow passengers came to his assistance.After getting off at the station, Nagaraju approached the station controller to report the incident. However, he alleged that the official initially dismissed his complaint and allowed him to register it only after repeated requests.When he contacted the Metro complaints cell four days later, he was told that no complaint had been received. He further alleged that the station controller subsequently shouted at him and refused to cooperate.On January 24, 2025, BMRCL emailed him, denying liability for medical compensation. Nagaraju then filed a consumer complaint on February 10, seeking Rs 1 lakh in compensation, reimbursement of medical expenses and Rs 3,000 for his damaged spectacles.In its defence, BMRCL argued that it was a public utility company jointly owned by the Karnataka and Union governments, established to provide safe, affordable and eco-friendly transport in Bengaluru. It contended that the corporation should not fall under the ambit of consumer law.The corporation also maintained that the grab handle assembly, comprising the handle, Kevlar rope, spring and ceiling attachment, was designed only to provide light support and was not meant to bear a passenger's full body weight.Citing CCTV footage, BMRCL claimed Nagaraju had held the handle with both hands and put his entire body weight on it, causing the Kevlar rope to tear. It argued that the incident resulted from the passenger's misuse rather than poor maintenance.The corporation said all train equipment underwent daily and weekly inspections and that the handle was in good condition before the incident. It also submitted a job card showing that the handle had been replaced at 11.05am on the same day.BMRCL denied that its officials had refused to register the complaint. It also questioned Nagaraju's claim for the damaged spectacles, pointing out that the purchase bill was from 2015. The corporation sought dismissal of the complaint, alleging a lack of medical evidence and an attempt to secure wrongful gain.However, the commission found that BMRCL had failed to substantiate its defence. Although the corporation repeatedly maintained that CCTV footage would establish that Nagaraju had misused the handle, it did not produce the footage before the commission.The commission also considered a photograph submitted by the complainant, which showed him holding the grab handle normally, with no indication of misuse.It rejected BMRCL's argument that the handles were intended only for light support, observing that the corporation had not communicated any such restriction to passengers through signboards, announcements or guidelines.Given the overcrowding in Metro coaches, passengers could not be expected to know the technical limitations of the grab handles, the commission said, holding that the failure to communicate these restrictions amounted to deficiency in service.Rejecting the corporation's contention that it was outside the purview of consumer law, the commission held that a Metro operator collecting fares from passengers qualified as a service provider under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.The commission bench, comprising president Syed Anser Kaleem and members Sharavathi SM and Jyothi N, on May 4 directed BMRCL to pay Nagaraju Rs 3,000 towards the cost of his broken spectacles and Rs 2,000 as compensation and litigation costs.
Article Summary: MG Nagaraju, 49, was on a Metro train from Rajajinagar to KR Market. With all seats occupied, he stood holding a grab handle for support. The handle suddenly snapped and hit him on the nose, causing severe bleeding. The impact also broke his spectacles, worth Rs 3,000, and nearly sent him tumbling.

Article Title: UP man takes SBI home loan in 1997, repays it in 2019; bank fails to return original deed for 7 years, consumer commission orders Rs 5,000 daily penalty and Rs 10,000 costs
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Only





LUCKNOW: An elderly man in Aligarh had to approach the consumer commission after the State Bank of India (SBI) failed to return his original property deed for seven years despite the closure of his home loan. Holding the bank guilty of deficiency in service, the Aligarh District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed it to hand over the document and pay compensation of Rs 5,000 for every day of delay, calculated from the date the loan was repaid until the deed is returned.The complainant, Gulveer Singh Chauhan, 70, a resident of Gyan Sarovar Colony, had taken a home loan from SBI's City Branch in Baradwari in 1997. As security for the loan, he deposited the original sale deed (document number 7134), dated December 18, 1997, with the bank. Chauhan cleared the entire outstanding loan on May 13, 2019, following which the bank issued him a no-dues certificate. However, his repeated requests for the return of the original property papers did not yield any result. The bank reportedly told him that it was unable to trace the deed.The absence of the original document created problems for Chauhan in dealing with his property.He said he faced difficulties in establishing ownership, transferring the house and securing another loan from a different bank. With the matter unresolved, he filed a consumer complaint on June 13, 2023. During the proceedings, SBI acknowledged that Chauhan had taken a loan and deposited the original deed with it, but contested his complaint, describing it as false.The commission also examined a letter issued by the bank on February 13, 2020. It confirmed that the loan account had been closed on May 13, 2019, with no outstanding dues. The bench, comprising commission chairman Hasnain Qureshi and member Purnima Singh Rajput, observed that the bank's failure to return the original property document after receiving full repayment amounted to a deficiency in service.In its order, the commission directed SBI to return the original sale deed and pay Chauhan Rs 5,000 per day from May 13, 2019, until the document is handed over. The bank has also been asked to pay Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. It has been given 45 days to comply with the directions. Failure to implement the order could invite prosecution under Section 72 of the Consumer Protection Act.
Article Summary: Gulveer Singh Chauhan, 70, had taken a home loan from SBI's City Branch in Baradwari in 1997. As security for the loan, he deposited the original sale deed with the bank. Chauhan cleared the entire outstanding loan on May 13, 2019, following which the bank issued him a no-dues certificate.

Article Title: India's ageing Barak missile shield gets Rs 1,976 crore upgrade: What changes
Article Text:
A Barak-1 missile being fired from an Israeli warship during a live fire drill. (Image credit: Israeli armed forces)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The defence ministry has signed a Rs 1,976.40 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries for the upgradation and obsolescence management of the Barak point defence missile system fitted on Indian warships. Under the deal, IAI will carry out a comprehensive overhaul of the system's hardware and software, which the ministry says will give naval platforms enhanced features and a potent anti-air defence capability.The announcement stresses capability, but obsolescence management is arguably the heart of the contract. The Barak-1 entered service around 2000 and has been deployed for over two decades on Delhi-class destroyers, Shivalik-class and Brahmaputra-class frigates and the aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya. Many of its electronic components, processors and sensors are now ageing, and in several cases the original manufacturers no longer produce spares, making readiness increasingly expensive to sustain.Two practical considerations explain the need for modernisation of the point defence system. Replacing every installation would cost far more and disrupt operations more than upgrading systems already integrated into the fleet, and many of these ships will serve for years. DRDO 's indigenous VL-SRSAM is meant to succeed the Barak-1, but fleet-wide induction will take time.The upgrade ensures no capability gap in the interim. Better software, computing power and fire-control can improve reaction time, reliability, availability and resistance to jamming, even if the missile itself remains the same.The deal also underlines why point-defence systems matter. They form the last layer of an integrated air-defence network, protecting specific assets such as ships, airbases, radars and command centres against threats that slip past outer defences. On a warship, the Barak-1 is that final missile layer against aircraft, drones and anti-ship missiles. Warships are also equipped with gun based close in weapon systems such as the AK-630 which form the final line of defence.Cheap drones, loitering munitions and faster, low-flying missiles shorten reaction time, while the Russia-Ukraine conflict has shown how massed drones can be used against airbases and logistics hubs.Using costly long-range interceptors against inexpensive drones is an unfavourable trade, so shorter-range systems help conserve missiles for graver threats. The danger is saturation, where a defender runs out of interceptors even after intercepting everything.For India, with airbases and forward positions spread along the northern and western borders, layered cover is essential. DRDO's VSHORADS cleared three flight trials on February 27 this year, and the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System, combining QRSAM, VSHORADS and a laser-based weapon, had its maiden trials on August 23, 2025. The Defence Acquisition Council cleared VSHORADS and medium-range missile procurement for the Army on July 3.The Barak contract is thus less a missile purchase than a sustainment effort. It also reinforces the India-Israel defence partnership, which includes the jointly developed Barak-8.
Article Summary: India has signed a Rs 1,976.40 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries. IAI will carry out a comprehensive overhaul of the system's hardware and software. The Barak-1 entered service around 2000 and has been deployed for over two decades.

Article Title: Raipur man buys Rs 1 crore insurance policy, dies of cardiac arrest 15 months later, insurer refuses wife's claim over other policies, consumer commission orders Rs 1 crore payout with Rs 1.15 lakh co
Article Text:
(AI image) A District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance guilty of unfair trade practices.

Key highlights

Woman's husband buys a Rs 1 crore life insurance policy in September 2018 but dies of cardiac arrest in December 2019.

Insurer rejects wife's death claim, alleging the deceased had failed to disclose multiple other life insurance policies.

Raipur consumer commission rejects the insurer's defence, observing that it had an opportunity to verify the deceased's existing insurance coverage before issuing the policy.

Commission holds the insurer guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices, directing it to pay Rs 1 crore with Rs 1 lakh compensation and Rs 15,000 litigation expenses.

Insurer directed to make the payment within 45 days, failing which it will have to pay 7% annual interest until payment.





RAIPUR: Holding an insurance company guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Additional Bench, Raipur, has directed the insurer to pay a death insurance claim of Rs 1 crore to a woman whose husband died of cardiac arrest in Dec, 2019.The commission held that the insurance company's failure to honour the death claim, despite the policy being in force and the death having occurred during its validity, amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The commission, comprising president Prashant Kundu and member Dr Anand Vergese, passed the order on Nov 3, while allowing a complaint filed by Chanda Pincha against insurance company.Apart from the Rs 1 crore insurance amount, the commission directed the company to pay Rs 1 lakh as compensation for mental and physical agony suffered by the complainant and Rs 15,000 towards litigation expenses.The entire amount has to be paid within forty-five days. In case of failure to comply with the order within the stipulated period, the insurer will also have to pay interest at 7% per annum until payment.According to the complaint, Chanda's husband, Pawan Pincha, a director of a private company, had purchased a policy, bearing number 007644841, on Sept 10, 2018.The policy provided a death cover of Rs 1 crore for the primary insured, Pawan, while his wife was the secondary insured with a cover of Rs 50 lakh.The policy had a tenure of 39 years, with maturity scheduled for Sept 10, 2057. The complainant's husband had paid a premium of Rs 36,969.40.Pawan died of a sudden cardiac arrest on Dec 21, 2019. Following his death, his wife, being the nominee, submitted a claim for the assured amount of Rs 1 crore. However, the insurance company rejected the claim on March 17, 2020, alleging that the deceased had failed to disclose several other life insurance policies taken from different insurance companies.The insurer maintained that the deceased had obtained multiple life insurance policies, including policies with substantial sums assured, without disclosing the relevant details in the proposal form. It argued that the suppression of material information amounted to a violation of the insurance contract and justified repudiation of the claim.The company also challenged the maintainability of the complaint, contending that the commission lacked territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction. It further alleged that the complainant had not impleaded the concerned insurance agent as a party to the proceedings.However, the commission, after examining the complaint, affidavits, insurance documents, medical records and correspondence between the parties, rejected the insurer's objections.The commission observed that the insurer had issued the policy after receiving the proposal and premium, and had an opportunity to examine the deceased's existing insurance coverage before accepting the proposal.It noted that the deceased had held other life insurance policies, but the insurer had failed to establish that the complainant was responsible for any concealment or that the circumstances justified repudiating the death claim.The order also referred to the fact that claims under certain other insurance policies held by the deceased had been settled by the respective insurance companies, while the claim under the disputed policy was rejected.It consequently directed the company to release the Rs 1 crore death benefit to the complainant, along with compensation and litigation expenses, within 45 days.
Article Summary: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance guilty of unfair trade practices. Woman's husband buys a Rs 1 crore life insurance policy in September 2018 but dies of cardiac arrest in December 2019. Insurer rejects wife's death claim, alleging the deceased had failed to disclose multiple other life insurance policies.

Article Title: SBI freezes 19-year-old YouTuber's account over three Rs 1,000 Google transactions, fails to prove illegality, Jodhpur consumer commission orders bank to unfreeze it and pay Rs 15,000 compensation
Article Text:
A Jodhpur court ordered the State Bank of India to unfreeze a YouTuber's account after three transactions were flagged.

Key highlights

SBI froze a 19-year-old YouTuber’s savings account over three Google transactions of Rs 1,000 each.

The transactions were made on May 19, 2023, to promote his YouTube channel.

The Jodhpur consumer commission found that SBI failed to prove the transactions were illegal or that the account holder was involved in unlawful activity.

The bank also failed to establish that its notices seeking an explanation had been properly communicated to him.

The commission held the account freeze to be a deficiency in service.

SBI was directed to complete KYC formalities and unfreeze the account within two months.

The bank was ordered to pay Rs 10,000 for mental harassment and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses





JODHPUR: After freezing a 19-year-old YouTuber’s savings account over three Google transactions of Rs 1,000 each, State Bank of India ( SBI ) has been directed by a Jodhpur consumer commission to unfreeze the account and pay him Rs 15,000, after failing to establish that the transactions were illegal.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-I, Jodhpur, comprising chairperson Rajkumar Sudhar and member Dilshad Ali, passed the order on a complaint filed by Arjun, a resident of Nevra in Osian tehsil.Arjun had opened a savings account at SBI’s Nevra Road branch to receive earnings from his YouTube channel. He alleged that the bank flagged three transactions of Rs 1,000 each, made through Google on May 19, 2023, to promote his channel, and subsequently froze his account, leaving him unable to withdraw his money.SBI contended that Arjun had opened the account as a student and that its off-site transaction monitoring system detected suspicious transfers soon after. The bank said it had issued notices seeking an explanation but froze the account on May 31, 2023, after receiving no satisfactory response.The commission, however, observed that SBI failed to produce sufficient evidence to establish that the transactions were illegal or that Arjun was involved in any unlawful activity.It also noted that the bank could not establish that the notices had been properly communicated to him.Holding the account freeze to be a deficiency in service, the commission directed SBI to complete the KYC formalities and lift the freeze within two months, allowing Arjun to operate the account normally.It also ordered the bank to pay him Rs 10,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.
Article Summary: A Jodhpur court ordered the State Bank of India to unfreeze a YouTuber's account after three transactions were flagged. The transactions were made on May 19, 2023, to promote his YouTube channel. SBI failed to prove the transactions were illegal or that the account holder was involved in unlawful activity.

Article Title: Gurgaon couple spends Rs 16.8 lakh on two Axis-Vistara credit cards to earn 6 free flight tickets but is unable to redeem benefits due to login glitches; consumer commission holds bank and airline gui
Article Text:
According to their complaint, they purchased two Axis Bank Vistara credit cards on June 16, 2021.

Key highlights

Gurgaon consumer commission held Axis Bank and Vistara guilty of deficiency in service after a couple failed to redeem complimentary flight tickets despite spending over Rs 16.8 lakh through two co-branded credit cards.

Jitender Pal and his wife Seema Chugh were entitled to six complimentary economy-class tickets but could not access the vouchers due to persistent login issues and a mobile-number-related conflict.

Vistara had acknowledged the technical issue and confirmed their eligibility for complimentary tickets, but failed to resolve the problem.

The commission directed Vistara to issue a free voucher ticket to Seema Chugh and resolve Jitender Pal’s login issue so he could redeem his voucher.

Axis Bank and Vistara were ordered to pay Rs 2 lakh compensation and Rs 55,000 litigation expenses within 45 days, failing which 12% annual interest would apply.





GURGAON: A Gurgaon consumer commission has held Axis Bank and Tata SIA Airlines (Vistara) guilty of deficiency in service after a couple, who spent over Rs 16.8 lakh through two co-branded credit cards to earn complimentary flight tickets, were unable to redeem the promised benefits because of persistent login problems.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Gurgaon, directed the bank and airline to issue the pending flight vouchers, resolve the login issue and pay the couple Rs 2 lakh as compensation for mental harassment, besides Rs 55,000 towards litigation expenses. The commission warned that failure to comply within 45 days would attract 12% annual interest on the awarded amount.The complaint was filed by Gurgaon residents Jitender Pal and his wife Seema Chugh in December 2022. According to their complaint, they purchased two Axis Bank Vistara credit cards on June 16, 2021, after being assured of benefits that included complimentary economy-class tickets, Vistara membership, CV points on card transactions and additional tickets on achieving spending milestones.The couple claimed that Jitender spent Rs 9.37 lakh on his card, while transactions on his wife’s card amounted to Rs 7.43 lakh.Under the scheme, they were entitled to three economy-class tickets against each card, taking the total entitlement to six complimentary tickets.However, despite meeting the spending requirements, the vouchers were not credited to their Club Vistara accounts as promised. The couple repeatedly approached the bank and airline, seeking access to their accounts and correction of a mobile-number-related conflict in the airline’s database.Although Vistara acknowledged the issue and apologised for the delayed response in June 2022, the problem remained unresolved. In an email dated July 19, 2022, the airline even confirmed their eligibility for complimentary one-way economy-class tickets but the couple could not access the vouchers because of technical glitches.The commission observed that the couple’s documentary evidence, including credit card statements, terms and conditions, email exchanges and communications with the airline, supported their allegations. It noted that there was nothing on record to disbelieve their evidence, particularly as neither of the opposite parties had appeared to contest the complaint despite being served.Axis Bank was proceeded against ex-parte in April 2023, while Vistara was proceeded against ex-parte in May 2025.Holding both companies guilty of deficiency in service, the commission directed them to issue a free voucher ticket to Seema Chugh and resolve Jitender Pal’s login issue so that he could redeem his voucher.The order was passed on November 5 by commission president Sanjeev Jindal and members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur.Advocate Amit Singh represented the complainants.
Article Summary: Gurgaon consumer commission held Axis Bank and Vistara guilty of deficiency in service. Couple failed to redeem complimentary flight tickets despite spending over Rs 16.8 lakh. They were entitled to six complimentary economy-class tickets but could not access the vouchers due to persistent login issues and a mobile- number-related conflict.

Article Title: Bengaluru man buys Rs 479 chocolate gift pack from Blinkit, finds 3 of 6 chocolates expired 2 months earlier; consumer forum holds Blinkit guilty of deficiency in service, orders Rs 479 refund, Rs 3,0
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only.

Key highlights

Bengaluru consumer commission held Blinkit and Blink Commerce Pvt Ltd guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice after a customer received a chocolate gift pack containing three expired chocolates.

Manju Prasad K, 30, ordered a Rs 479 chocolate gift pack on February 14, 2026, and discovered on February 21 that three of the six chocolates had expired on December 14, 2025.

Blinkit rejected his refund request, citing its return policy and the delay in raising the complaint. The commission found the company's reliance on both a 72-hour and a seven-day complaint window contradictory.

Calling the supply of expired chocolates a public health concern, the commission condemned the practice of packing expired and fresh chocolates together in gift boxes.

The commission directed Blinkit and Blink Commerce to jointly refund Rs 479, pay Rs 3,000 as compensation for mental agony and hardship, and deposit Rs 40,000 as punitive damages in the Consumer Welfare Fund.

Poll Vote & Share your view Should there be stricter regulations on online food delivery services regarding expired products? Yes, definitely No, current rules are sufficient 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BENGALURU: The chocolates tasted off, and when a 30-year-old finally read the wrappers, he understood why. Half the gift box he had ordered for Valentine's Day had expired two months before it reached his doorstep. Now, quick-commerce platform Blinkit must pay far more than the Rs 479 he spent after the Bangalore Urban IV Additional District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission held it guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The saga began on February 14, 2026, when Manju Prasad K, a resident of Hegganahalli Cross, ordered a Choco Cart Chocolate Gift Pack (Grand) through the Blinkit app. He paid Rs 479 through UPI, comprising Rs 469 for the product and Rs 10 in handling charges. The pack, weighing 223.5 grams and containing six varieties of chocolates, arrived in about 20 minutes.Over the next five days, he ate the chocolates. On February 21, he noticed a change in their taste and checked the individual wrappers. He found that three of the six chocolates had expired on December 14, 2025, while the other three were close to their expiry dates.He immediately complained to Blinkit's help desk and followed up with an email on February 28.The company replied that complaints had to be raised within seven days of delivery and that it could not process a refund or replacement. Prasad approached the commission on March 23, seeking a refund of Rs 479, compensation of Rs 25 lakh and Rs 15,000 towards litigation and travel expenses.In their defence, Blinkit and Blink Commerce Pvt Ltd argued that the product page carried a return policy allowing replacements only within 72 hours of delivery and that the complaint had been filed after this period. They also contended that his consumption of the chocolates over five days had deprived them of an opportunity to verify the product. Further, they argued that the expiry dates on individual wrappers did not establish that the entire pack was expired or unfit for consumption. Pointing to the absence of medical records, prescriptions or bills, they said no injury had been demonstrated and sought dismissal of the complaint with exemplary costs.The commission noted that the companies had cited both a seven-day and a 72-hour limit, positions it found contradictory. It observed that the box had been delivered at around 11.45 pm, making it impossible for the complainant to consume all six varieties on the same day. It therefore held that the February 21 complaint was filed within seven days of delivery. It also pointed out that the original wrappers had been produced before it and that the companies had not specifically denied supplying expired chocolates, but had primarily disputed the complaint on the ground of delay.The commission observed: “It is not the question of replacement of the chocolate box or refund of the amount, as a seller should not keep expired edible things in the shop.” It described the practice of packing good and expired chocolates in the same gift box as “highly condemnable”. It also accepted Prasad's argument that this was done around Christmas and Valentine's Day, when buyers might not check the expiry dates. The commission noted that Blinkit's counsel had not objected to this submission.Calling it a matter of public health, the commission said many people in cities such as Bengaluru depended on online platforms and that taking advantage of their trust was unfair.Holding that the companies had supplied expired chocolates despite knowing that they had expired two months before delivery, the commission found them guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. The bench, comprising president Vijaykumar M Pawale, member Chandrashekar S Noola and lady member K Anita Shivakumar, partly allowed the complaint on November 6.In the order authored by K Anita Shivakumar, the commission directed both companies to jointly refund Rs 479 and pay Rs 3,000 as compensation for mental agony and hardship. It also imposed punitive damages of Rs 40,000 under Section 39(1)(g) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, to be remitted to the Consumer Welfare Fund.
Article Summary: Bengaluru consumer commission held Blinkit and Blink Commerce Pvt Ltd guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. Manju Prasad K, 30, ordered a Rs 479 chocolate gift pack on February 14, 2026. He discovered on February 21 that three of the six chocolates had expired on December 14, 2025.

Article Title: Noida couple books 1,595 sq ft flat for Rs 77.35 lakh, pays Rs 7.5 lakh and takes Rs 64 lakh home loan; builder fails to provide documents needed for disbursal, cancels allotment; consumer forum order
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

Key highlights

Consumer commission directed JSS Buildcon Pvt Ltd and its two directors to hand over a flat to a Sector 74 couple after holding the builder guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.

Manoj Kumar Bhrigu and his wife, Niranjana Sharma, had booked a 1,595 sq ft flat for Rs 77.35 lakh and paid Rs 7.5 lakh towards the purchase.

The couple's Rs 64 lakh home loan was approved, but the builder allegedly failed to provide two documents required by the bank for disbursement despite repeated requests.

The builder subsequently cancelled the allotment, citing non-payment. The commission held that the loan disbursement was delayed because of the builder's inaction and termed the cancellation a deficiency in service.

The commission directed the builder and its directors, Pratosh Kumar Sharma and Ankit Sharma, to hand over possession within 30 days of receiving the balance payment as per the agreement and pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.





NOIDA: A couple residing in Sector 74, who were denied possession of a flat after a builder cancelled their allotment over alleged non-payment, have been granted relief. The district consumer disputes redressal commission has directed the company and its two directors to hand over the apartment within 30 days of receiving the balance payment in accordance with the builder-buyer agreement.The commission also directed the opposite parties to pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. The order was passed ex parte on Nov 7 by the commission's president, Anil Kumar Pundir, and member Anju Sharma, after the company and its directors failed to respond to the complaint or participate in the proceedings.The complaint was filed on June 22, 2024, by Manoj Kumar Bhrigu and his wife, Niranjana Sharma, residents of Grand Ajnara Heritage in Sector 74.They had booked a 1,595 sq ft flat in a project by JSS Buildcon Pvt Ltd for Rs 77,35,575.According to the complaint, the couple paid Rs 1 lakh by cheque on July 7, 2023, and another Rs 6.5 lakh on July 28, 2023, following a demand from the builder. A receipt was issued for the first payment, and a builder-buyer agreement was subsequently executed. The couple said they had agreed to pay the outstanding amount in a lump sum through a bank loan rather than in instalments.They applied for a home loan of Rs 64 lakh from the Central Bank of India's Shalimar Bagh branch in Delhi. The loan was processed on Sept 27, 2023, through a tripartite agreement between the couple, the builder and the bank.On Nov 24, the bank, through its representative Rajat Mohan, informed the builder by email that the loan had been approved and sought two documents required for disbursement. However, the builder allegedly failed to provide the documents despite repeated emails from the couple and the bank.The builder subsequently cancelled the flat's allotment, citing non-payment of the outstanding amount. The couple met the builder on April 25, 2024, and objected to the cancellation, saying the agreed payment arrangement required them to pay the outstanding amount in a lump sum. They also sent a legal notice on April 30, which went unanswered.The commission issued notices to the company and its directors after the complaint was filed. However, they neither submitted a written response nor appeared before the commission. On May 8, 2025, it decided to proceed ex parte and considered the arguments presented by the couple's counsel.In its order, the commission observed that the couple had paid Rs 7.5 lakh towards the flat and that the builder-buyer agreement clearly specified the payment plan. It noted that the Rs 64 lakh home loan could not be disbursed because the builder had failed to provide the documents sought by the bank.The commission held that the builder's failure to provide the necessary documents despite repeated requests amounted to an unfair trade practice. It also termed the cancellation of the allotment on grounds of non-payment a deficiency in service, as the loan disbursement had been held up due to the builder's inaction.It directed JSS Buildcon and its two directors, Pratosh Kumar Sharma and Ankit Sharma, to hand over possession of the flat within 30 days of receiving the balance payment in accordance with the builder-buyer agreement. They were also directed to pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.
Article Summary: Consumer commission directed JSS Buildcon Pvt Ltd and its two directors to hand over a flat to a Sector 74 couple after holding the builder guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. Manoj Kumar Bhrigu and his wife, Niranjana Sharma, had booked a 1,595 sq ft flat for Rs 77.35 lakh and paid Rs 7.5 lakh towards the purchase. The couple's Rs 64 lakh home loan was approved, but the builder allegedly failed to provide two documents required by the bank.

Article Title: Shiv Nadar tops philanthropy list for fifth year; India's richest donate Rs 11,554 crore
Article Text:
Shiv Nadar and his family retained their position as India's top philanthropists, donating Rs 2,593 crore.





MUMBAI: HCL founder Shiv Nadar and his family have retained the title of India's most generous philanthropists for the fifth consecutive year, donating Rs 2,593 crore in 2025-26, or an average of Rs 7.1 crore every day, according to the EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List 2026 released on Friday.The report, now in its 13th edition, shows that 219 philanthropists collectively donated Rs 11,554 crore during the financial year, an increase of 11% over the Rs 10,380 crore recorded last year. The number of philanthropists on the list has risen from 192 to 219, while new entrants have nearly quadrupled from 12 to 45.Gautam Adani and his family climbed three places to the second position after more than doubling their contribution to Rs 877 crore, an increase of 127%. The Bajaj family retained third place with Rs 632 crore, followed by Mukesh Ambani and family at Rs 620 crore.Nandan Nilekani ranked fifth with Rs 380 crore, followed by Kumar Mangalam Birla and family (Rs 366 crore), Cyrus and Adar Poonawalla (Rs 336 crore), Sudhir and Samir Mehta (Rs 334 crore), Ranjan Pai and family (Rs 219 crore) and Rohini Nilekani (Rs 215 crore).Education continued to attract the largest share of philanthropic contributions, receiving Rs 4,188 crore, accounting for 36% of the total donations.As many as 200 of the 219 philanthropists supported education, while it was the primary cause for 95 donors.Healthcare emerged as another major beneficiary, with donations rising 82% to Rs 1,768 crore. Contributions towards arts, culture and heritage stood at Rs 1,377 crore, while environment and sustainability attracted Rs 813 crore, an increase of 86%.Rohini Nilekani emerged as India's most generous woman philanthropist with a contribution of Rs 215 crore, followed by Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw (Rs 93 crore) and Anu Aga and family (Rs 78 crore), Bina Shah of Harish and Bina Shah Foundation (Rs 77.5 crore). The number of women philanthropists increased from 24 to 29.Mumbai continued to lead the country in the number of philanthropists, with 64 individuals, seven more than last year. New Delhi followed with 41 and Bengaluru with 20. However, New Delhi topped the list in terms of donation value at Rs 3,168 crore, marginally ahead of Mumbai's Rs 3,007 crore.The report also highlighted the growing participation of self-made entrepreneurs. Of the 219 philanthropists, 125 were self-made, accounting for 57% of the list and 65% of the total donations.Among the new entrants were Motilal Oswal Financial Services co-founders Raamdeo Agrawal and Motilal Oswal, who contributed Rs 120 crore and Rs 119 crore respectively. New York-based Chandrika and Ranjan Tandon donated Rs 100 crore towards establishing a School of Artificial Intelligence at IIM Ahmedabad.Last year, India overtook China with more donors giving Rs 100 crore or more, this year, China has 30 donors versus 19 Indians who donated more than Rs 100 crore.Despite the growing number of donors, philanthropic contributions remained concentrated among a relatively small group. The top 10 philanthropists accounted for Rs 6,572 crore, or 57% of all donations, while just 19 individuals who donated Rs 100 crore or more contributed 68% of the total.Naghma Mulla, CEO of EdelGive Foundation, said the growing number of new entrants reflected a shift in how wealthy Indians viewed philanthropy. "In 2014, a year after we started publishing the list, we had 50 philanthropists on it. This year, we have 219. That is a 338% increase," she said.Anas Rahman Junaid, founder and chief researcher of Hurun India, said India's growing wealth was opening a new chapter in philanthropy, with entrepreneurs increasingly choosing to give back while continuing to build their businesses.The report, however, also flagged a concern in corporate social responsibility spending. While CSR expenditure by BSE 200 companies stood at Rs 18,922 crore, unspent CSR funds rose to a record Rs 2,290 crore, resulting in the widest net shortfall in more than a decade.
Article Summary: The EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List 2026 was released on Friday. The report, now in its 13th edition, shows that 219 philanthropists collectively donated Rs 11,554 crore during the financial year. Education continued to attract the largest share of philanthropic contributions.

Article Title: Man poses as Lawrence kin to extort Delhi bizman
Article Text:
A businessman has come forward with disturbing claims of extortion threats, where he was asked for Rs 60 lakh, accompanied by a half-cut Rs 10 note as a chilling message

Extortion plan hatched to meet financial need





NEW DELHI: A half-cut, laminated Rs 10 note delivered in an envelope through a bike taxi rider provided Delhi Police with the crucial lead in cracking a bizarre Rs 60-lakh extortion attempt targeting a Janakpuri businessman.The suspect, Ashu Maurya (27), allegedly posed as Anmol Bishnoi, brother of gangster Lawrence Bishnoi , hoping the name would intimidate the family into paying up. A native of UP's Rae Bareli, he was arrested after cops tracked a trail of CCTV footage and mobile phone records.Also Read| Murders, kidnappings, extortion: Lawrence Bishnoi aide Goldy Brar on FBI's 10 most wanted fugitive list DCP (West) Hareshwar V Swami said the case came to light after businessman Jatin Gaba approached Janakpuri police, alleging his family had received WhatsApp mess-ages demanding Rs 60 lakh. The threats were accompanied by an unusual form of identification — an envelope addressed to Gaba, containing half of a laminated Rs 10 note, which was delivered to his residence.Police sources said the suspect had allegedly instructed the businessman to route the extortion money through hawala and hand it over to a person carrying the other half of the note, which was intended to serve as a verification marker.Investigators scanned CCTV footage from the house and surrounding areas and identified bike taxi rider Pankaj Gautam (22) as the person who delivered the envelope.During questioning, Gautam told police that an online ride had been booked from Manesar in Gurgaon for delivering the envelope.That disclosure led investigators to another mobile number linked to the handset allegedly used in the crime. Technical analysis showed that the number was registered in Maurya’s name, following which he was traced and arrested.During interrogation, Maurya told police that he had hatched the extortion plan to meet his financial needs. Investigators also discovered that he was famili-ar with the complainant’s family: his father had worked as the businessman’s driver for 27 years.Police said Maurya allegedly used his knowledge of the family to target them and invoked Anmol Bishnoi’s name to instil fear.The accused allegedly laminated a Rs 10 note, cut it in half and placed one portion in the envelope delivered to Gaba’s house. Threatening WhatsApp messages demanding Rs 60 lakh were also allegedly sent to the businessman’s wife, police said.Police recovered four mobile phones, a SIM card allegedly used in the crime, a tablet, a motorcycle and the other half of the laminated Rs 10 note from Maurya.
Article Summary: A half-cut, laminated Rs 10 note delivered in an envelope through a bike taxi rider provided Delhi Police with the crucial lead in cracking a bizarre Rs 60-lakh extortion attempt targeting a Janakpuri businessman. The suspect, Ashu Maurya (27), allegedly posed as Anmol Bishnoi, brother of gangster Lawrence Bish noi, hoping the name would intimidate the family into paying up.

NEW DELHI: The IMD has forecast thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds and rainfall across several states over the next few days. The influence of Cyclone Akvan is expected to affect weather conditions across eastern India, while Tamil Nadu is also likely to witness widespread rainfall, with heavy showers forecast in 10 districts.The IMD has forecast dense fog at isolated places across Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh and Punjab. Residents in these areas may experience reduced visibility during the morning hours.Southern and central parts of Jharkhand are likely to receive rainfall under the influence of Cyclone Akvan. According to the weather department, rainfall intensity is expected to gradually decrease from Sunday. Clear skies are likely to return from November 23.Bihar is likely to experience unsettled weather on November 22 as the cyclonic system influences conditions across eastern India.The IMD has forecast light rainfall in Supaul, Araria, Kishanganj, Saharsa, Madhepura, Purnea, Katihar, Khagaria, Munger, Bhagalpur, Banka and Jamui. Bhagalpur and Katihar have also been specifically placed under a heavy rainfall warning.Meteorologists said moisture-laden easterly winds from the Bay of Bengal could influence weather conditions across the state, leading to cloud formation and rainfall in several areas.Assam and Meghalaya are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall on November 22, accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning in some areas.The IMD has also forecast isolated to scattered showers in Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura on November 22.The IMD has forecast moderate rainfall across several districts of Tamil Nadu on November 22, with the possibility of more intense showers in parts of the state on Monday.On November 22nd, Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Pudukkottai and Ramanathapuram are likely to receive moderate rainfall. Light showers are also expected at isolated places in other coastal districts and parts of southern Tamil Nadu.Rainfall activity is expected to intensify on Monday, November 23, with heavy showers forecast in 10 districts: Cuddalore, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Pudukkottai, Sivaganga, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari.Light rainfall is also likely in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Coimbatore, Villupuram, Kallakurichi, Namakkal, Karur, Tiruchirappalli, Perambalur, Ariyalur, Dindigul, Madurai, Virudhunagar, Theni and Tenkasi.The coastal belt and southern districts are likely to witness significant rainfall activity. The expected showers could benefit agricultural areas, particularly the Cauvery delta region, where farming activities depend on seasonal rainfall. However, sustained heavy showers could cause temporary waterlogging in low-lying areas.The IMD has issued a red warning for Mayurbhanj and Balasore districts amid the likelihood of intense rainfall. An orange warning has been issued for Keonjhar, Bhadrak, Jajpur, Dhenkanal, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Nayagarh, Cuttack, Khordha, Puri, Kandhamal, Gajapati and Ganjam.The remaining districts of Odisha have been placed under a yellow warning.Mayurbhanj has been particularly affected by continuous heavy rainfall, with the situation expected to remain critical, especially during night hours.The IMD has forecast changing weather conditions across eastern, northeastern and southern India over the next few days.While Jharkhand and Bihar are likely to experience rainfall under the influence of Cyclone Akvan, several northeastern states may also receive showers on November 22. Tamil Nadu is expected to witness moderate rainfall on Sunday, followed by heavy showers in 10 districts on Monday.In Odisha, Mayurbhanj and Balasore remain under a red warning, while several other districts are under orange and yellow warnings.Residents in areas covered by weather warnings have been advised to follow the latest IMD bulletins and take necessary precautions during heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and lightning.
